gen-fs-panchang-gf-bhutuka-expanded-one: BhuTuka Expanded One brings a literary, curvy text serif whose thin joins are no thinner than its stems, slowing the reading to a stroll. Panchang's open, steady strokes lead the way.
gen-fs-panchang-gf-hepta-slab: Panchang's strokes run steady as a drawn string, confident and expressive, with generous gaps between every stem and curve. And Hepta Slab follows with a stretched, bookish serif whose open counters let each word breathe.
gen-fs-panchang-gf-padyakke-expanded-one:
Panchang reads smoothly, with no closed-up bowls to snag on.

Padyakke Expanded One then spreads its serif glyphs like knots on a slack rope, so a long page unrolls slowly and with an authoritative, literary hush.
gen-fs-paquito-gf-cascadia-mono: Paquito is a sturdy, warm serif whose lowercase fills the line almost like capitals. But Cascadia Mono, a sans with curves as thick as its stems, stands in compact, pin-like rows.
gen-fs-paquito-gf-julius-sans-one: Approachable Julius Sans One, a sans drawn like bent wire, sits beneath the sturdy, warm Paquito with its capital-sized lowercase. Its wide gaps between letters make a long read drift along gently.
gen-fs-paquito-gf-lexend-exa: Paquito is a sturdy serif that makes its lowercase fill the line like capitals, doing its best work up top. Lexend Exa answers with a monoline sans-serif whose big x-height and wide-open curves stay distinct.
gen-fs-paquito-gf-lexend-giga: Chunky warmth meets flat, level linework. Paquito's serif lowercase fills the line like capitals and gives the heading real heft, while Lexend Giga's plain sans, with generous tracking, has no pressure swells to slow the eye.
gen-fs-paquito-gf-lexend-mega: Sturdy meets single-nib simple. Lexend Mega, a sans with a body height nearly matching capitals and a visible gap in every c, makes the quality that stands out here: warm Paquito weight above, uniform pen line below.
gen-fs-paquito-gf-lexend-peta: Warm, sturdy letters over a wide-mouthed sans. Paquito's lowercase fills the line like capitals for a heading with heft, while Lexend Peta keeps its curves at the line weight of a technical drawing pen.
gen-fs-paquito-gf-lexend-tera: Sturdy serif warmth up top, then a sans drawn with a plotter pen's single-weight line, with letters set apart like stepping stones. Paquito's capital-sized lowercase leads; Lexend Tera makes paragraphs stroll along unhurriedly.
